competencies.name: Plasma and blood functions
competencies.can: State the three functional categories of blood, transport, regulation, and protection, and name the major plasma proteins and the function of each.

competencies.name: Hematocrit and formed elements
competencies.can: Define hematocrit and interpret a value as normal or abnormal in the context of anemia and dehydration.

competencies.name: Erythrocyte structure and hemoglobin
competencies.can: Relate the biconcave shape and absent nucleus of the erythrocyte to its function and describe how the four heme groups of hemoglobin carry oxygen.

competencies.name: Erythropoiesis and its regulation
competencies.can: Trace the erythropoietin negative feedback loop from tissue hypoxia to increased red cell production and state the nutrients required.

competencies.name: Red cell destruction and bilirubin
competencies.can: Trace the fate of hemoglobin after red cell breakdown and explain how failure to clear bilirubin produces jaundice.

competencies.name: Leukocytes
competencies.can: Match neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils to their defensive function and to the condition that raises each.

competencies.name: Hemostasis
competencies.can: Order the three phases of hemostasis, vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, and coagulation, and identify the role of von Willebrand factor and thromboxane.

competencies.name: Coagulation cascade
competencies.can: Compare the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways to the common pathway and identify the roles of thrombin, fibrin, calcium, and vitamin K.

competencies.name: Clot limitation and fibrinolysis
competencies.can: Explain how anticoagulants and plasmin limit and remove a clot and predict the effect of a drug that blocks vitamin K or platelet aggregation.

competencies.name: ABO and Rh blood types
competencies.can: Predict agglutination for any donor and recipient ABO and Rh combination and explain the mechanism of hemolytic disease of the newborn.

competencies.name: Hematocrit and hemoglobin determination
competencies.can: Determine hematocrit and hemoglobin from a sample or simulation and evaluate the result against reference ranges.

competencies.name: Blood typing
competencies.can: Perform simulated ABO and Rh typing and determine compatible donor types for the result obtained.

competencies.name: Pacemaker potential
competencies.can: Explain the unstable pacemaker potential of the sinoatrial node by the funny current, calcium entry, and potassium exit and state what sets intrinsic heart rate.

competencies.name: Contractile cell action potential
competencies.can: Diagram the ventricular action potential and identify the ion movement responsible for the rapid upstroke, the plateau, and repolarization.

competencies.name: Conduction system
competencies.can: Trace an impulse through the sinoatrial node, internodal pathways, atrioventricular node, bundle of His, bundle branches, and Purkinje fibers and explain the purpose of the atrioventricular delay.

competencies.name: Cardiac refractory period
competencies.can: Explain why the long refractory period of cardiac muscle prevents tetanus and why that matters for pump function.

competencies.name: ECG waves and intervals
competencies.can: Label the P wave, QRS complex, T wave, PR interval, and QT interval and state the electrical event each represents.

competencies.name: ECG interpretation
competencies.can: Calculate heart rate from an ECG strip and identify sinus rhythm, tachycardia, bradycardia, and a first degree or complete heart block.

competencies.name: ECG recording
competencies.can: Record a lead II ECG, measure the intervals, and correlate each wave with the mechanical event that follows it.

competencies.name: Cardiac cycle
competencies.can: Order the phases of the cardiac cycle and state the pressure relationship that opens and closes the atrioventricular and semilunar valves in each phase.

competencies.name: Pressure volume loop
competencies.can: Label the four phases of a ventricular pressure volume loop and predict how the loop changes with increased preload, increased afterload, or increased contractility.

competencies.name: Heart sounds
competencies.can: Explain the origin of the first and second heart sounds and relate a murmur to valve stenosis or regurgitation by its timing.

competencies.name: Stroke volume and ejection fraction
competencies.can: Calculate stroke volume and ejection fraction from end diastolic and end systolic volumes and interpret a reduced ejection fraction.

competencies.name: Cardiac output
competencies.can: Calculate cardiac output and cardiac reserve and predict the effect of a change in heart rate or stroke volume on each.

competencies.name: Frank Starling relationship
competencies.can: State the Frank Starling law and explain how venous return and end diastolic volume determine the force of the next contraction.

competencies.name: Preload afterload and contractility
competencies.can: Distinguish preload, afterload, and contractility and predict how a change in each alters stroke volume.

competencies.name: Autonomic regulation of the heart
competencies.can: Explain how sympathetic and parasympathetic input alter heart rate and contractility at the receptor and second messenger level.

competencies.name: Heart sound and pulse correlation
competencies.can: Auscultate the heart sounds, locate the valve areas, and correlate the sounds with the pulse and with the cardiac cycle phases.

competencies.name: Pressure flow and resistance
competencies.can: Apply the relationship among flow, pressure gradient, and resistance and predict the effect of a change in vessel radius, blood viscosity, or vessel length on flow.

competencies.name: Vessel structure and function
competencies.can: Match arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules, and veins to their role in pressure buffering, resistance, exchange, and capacitance.

competencies.name: Arterial blood pressure
competencies.can: Define systolic, diastolic, pulse, and mean arterial pressure, calculate mean arterial pressure, and explain how it is determined by cardiac output and total peripheral resistance.

competencies.name: Local control of blood flow
competencies.can: Explain myogenic, metabolic, and endothelial control of arteriolar tone and predict the local flow response to increased tissue metabolism.

competencies.name: Capillary exchange and Starling forces
competencies.can: Identify the four Starling forces at a capillary and determine the net direction of fluid movement at the arterial and venous ends.

competencies.name: Edema
competencies.can: Explain how increased capillary hydrostatic pressure, reduced plasma protein, increased permeability, or lymphatic blockage each produce edema and match a clinical scenario to its mechanism.

competencies.name: Lymphatic return
competencies.can: State the volume of fluid the lymphatic system returns each day and trace lymph from an interstitial space to the subclavian vein.

competencies.name: Venous return
competencies.can: Explain the skeletal muscle pump, the respiratory pump, and venoconstriction and predict the effect of prolonged standing on venous return and stroke volume.

competencies.name: Blood pressure measurement
competencies.can: Measure blood pressure by auscultation, explain the origin of the Korotkoff sounds, and record the response to a postural or exercise challenge.

competencies.name: Baroreceptor reflex
competencies.can: Trace the baroreceptor reflex from the carotid sinus and aortic arch through the medulla to the heart and vessels and state the response to a fall in blood pressure.

competencies.name: Hormonal control of blood pressure
competencies.can: Describe the roles of angiotensin II, aldosterone, antidiuretic hormone, and atrial natriuretic peptide in long term blood pressure control.

competencies.name: Cardiovascular response to exercise
competencies.can: Predict the change in heart rate, stroke volume, cardiac output, total peripheral resistance, and regional blood flow distribution during moderate exercise.

competencies.name: Compensation in hemorrhage and shock
competencies.can: Sequence the compensatory responses to blood loss and explain the point at which compensation fails.

competencies.name: Functions and functional zones
competencies.can: State the functions of the respiratory system and distinguish the conducting zone from the respiratory zone by structure and by role in gas exchange.

competencies.name: Pressure gradients and airflow
competencies.can: Apply Boyle's law to inspiration and expiration and relate alveolar pressure to atmospheric pressure at each point in a quiet breath.

competencies.name: Intrapleural pressure
competencies.can: Explain why intrapleural pressure is subatmospheric and predict what happens to the lung and chest wall when the pleural seal is broken.

competencies.name: Compliance and elastic recoil
competencies.can: Define lung compliance and elastic recoil and predict the effect of fibrosis and of emphysema on each.

competencies.name: Surfactant and surface tension
competencies.can: Explain how surfactant lowers surface tension and why its absence causes alveolar collapse in the premature newborn.

competencies.name: Airway resistance
competencies.can: Identify the main determinant of airway resistance and predict the effect of bronchoconstriction, mucus, and sympathetic stimulation on airflow.

competencies.name: Lung volumes and capacities
competencies.can: Define tidal volume, inspiratory and expiratory reserve volume, residual volume, vital capacity, and total lung capacity and read each from a spirogram.

competencies.name: Obstructive and restrictive patterns
competencies.can: Use the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity to classify a spirometry result as obstructive or restrictive.

competencies.name: Alveolar ventilation and dead space
competencies.can: Calculate minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation and explain why slow deep breathing ventilates the alveoli better than rapid shallow breathing.

competencies.name: Spirometry
competencies.can: Record a spirogram, calculate the lung volumes and capacities available from it, and compare the results with predicted values.

competencies.name: Partial pressures
competencies.can: Apply Dalton's law to calculate the partial pressure of oxygen in inspired and alveolar air and state the normal partial pressures in alveolar air, arterial blood, and venous blood.

competencies.name: Diffusion at the respiratory membrane
competencies.can: Apply the determinants of diffusion to the respiratory membrane and predict the effect of edema, fibrosis, and emphysema on gas transfer.

competencies.name: Ventilation perfusion matching
competencies.can: Explain how local hypoxic vasoconstriction and bronchiolar responses match ventilation to perfusion and predict the consequence of a mismatch.

competencies.name: Oxygen transport and the oxyhemoglobin curve
competencies.can: Explain the sigmoid shape of the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve and state the physiological advantage of the steep and the flat portions.

competencies.name: Curve shifts
competencies.can: Predict the direction of the oxyhemoglobin curve shift produced by a change in pH, carbon dioxide, temperature, or 2,3 bisphosphoglycerate and state what the shift means for tissue oxygen delivery.

competencies.name: Carbon dioxide transport
competencies.can: Name the three forms in which carbon dioxide is carried, state the approximate percentage of each, and trace the chloride shift in a systemic capillary.

competencies.name: Bohr and Haldane effects
competencies.can: Distinguish the Bohr effect from the Haldane effect and explain how the two work together at the tissue and at the lung.

competencies.name: Oxygen content versus partial pressure
competencies.can: Distinguish oxygen content from oxygen partial pressure and saturation and explain why anemia and carbon monoxide poisoning reduce delivery differently.

competencies.name: Respiratory centers
competencies.can: Identify the medullary and pontine respiratory centers and explain how the basic breathing rhythm is generated and modified.

competencies.name: Chemoreceptor control
competencies.can: Compare central and peripheral chemoreceptors by stimulus and explain why carbon dioxide is the primary minute to minute drive to breathe.

competencies.name: Ventilation in exercise and at altitude
competencies.can: Predict the ventilatory response to exercise and to acute and chronic altitude exposure and explain the acclimatization changes.

competencies.name: Ventilatory response testing
competencies.can: Measure the change in breathing rate and depth after hyperventilation, breath holding, and rebreathing and explain each result by the change in carbon dioxide.
